findings.title: Charge all reserved sibling lists against one serialized-byte/node budget
findings.reason: Each sibling list checks n*minimum_record_bytes against the same remaining file tail, then allocates all n nodes before reading the first. A nested first-child chain can repeat that allocation at each of64 permitted levels while unread siblings from earlier levels still consume no bytes. The same padding can justify many allocations; the scene header node_budget may be INT_MAX and therefore does not bound it by the file. For example, a512MiB file can pass local binary96-byte checks for5million siblings at each level and allocate about320million52-byte Nodes (16.64GB) before the depth/truncation refusal. try_reserve only checks virtual reservation; resize writes the memory and can still exhaust/kill the process under overcommit.
findings.bounded_correction: Derive and charge a conservative cumulative node budget from serialized bytes/minimum record size, or reserve the bytes required by all pending siblings before accepting children. Check cumulative capacity/resource limits before allocation; retain valid node order and minimum-size boundary cases. Add a small/instrumented depth-amplification control proving reservations cannot exceed the conservative global budget. Do not execute unsafe multi-GB old allocation controls.
findings.evidence: Static correction-specific counterexample; no unsafe allocation was executed. Existing local tiny-file guards legitimately pass but do not cover this cumulative case.
